texts: After an arterial switch, neoaortic valve regurgitation is more common in DORV than after the switch for simple transposition: C.
In the Taussig-Bing heart the pulmonary root is often larger than the aortic root and the great vessels are side by side, so the new aortic root is more prone to dilate and leak.
Early mortality after DORV repair is now about 5 percent, AV septal defects raise the risk, and subaortic obstruction recurs in more than 10 percent of tunnel repairs.
In the picture, the switched DORV hotel's new orca mouth gurgles back more than the simple-transposition hotel's.
Memory hook: after the switch, the DORV mouth leaks more.
